children: Deepa Jewellers shares made a strong stock market debut on Tuesday, with the stock listing at Rs 221 on the NSE, a 24.86 percent premium to its IPO issue price of Rs 177 per share.

The Deepa Jewellers IPO had received robust investor demand, with the Rs 460-crore mainline issue subscribed 42.61 times by the close of bidding on September 3. Investors bid for 78.91 crore equity shares against 1.85 crore shares on offer, according to the stock exchange data.

Demand was particularly strong among non-institutional investors (NIIs), whose portion was subscribed 105.96 times. The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) quota was booked 37 times, while the retail investor portion received 18.55 times subscription.

The Deepa Jewellers IPO was open for subscription from September 1 to September 3, with a price band of Rs 168-177 per share. The company subsequently fixed the IPO issue price at the upper end of the band at Rs 177.

The public offer comprised a fresh issue worth Rs 250 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) worth Rs 210 crore, involving the sale of about 1.18 crore shares. At the upper end of the IPO price band, Deepa Jewellers was valued at a post-issue market capitalisation of around Rs 1,700 crore.

Ahead of the IPO, the company had raised Rs 138 crore from 14 anchor investors by allotting 77.91 lakh shares at Rs 177 apiece. The anchor book included Motilal Oswal Finvest, WhiteOak Capital, 360 ONE, Nomura Singapore, Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust and Citigroup, among others.

Deepa Jewellers plans to deploy the bulk of the fresh issue proceeds towards working capital requirements. Around Rs 215 crore has been earmarked for long-term working capital, including the procurement, maintenance and expansion of jewellery inventory, while the balance will be used for general corporate purposes.

Incorporated in 2016, Deepa Jewellers is a business-to-business jewellery company that designs, processes and supplies 22-karat hallmarked gold jewellery to retail chains and standalone stores. Its key markets include Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
